notes:
BLUEPRINT READ (6x upscale of 168x179 source, cross-checked against sibling double-pleat.jpg): the drawing is a detail view of the lower sleeve exterior showing a pointed tower placket with 1 button, a single-button barrel cuff, and exactly ONE red pleat line running vertically from the sleeve down into the cuff seam, positioned between the placket and the outer sleeve edge. The sibling cpleat-double blueprint shows TWO such lines, which independently confirms the count of one here. CONSISTENCY GATE: label 'Single Pleat' and description ('one small fold of fabric') agree with the drawing - no conflict.

CANDIDATE VERIFICATION (adversarial; inspected at 6x on the sleeve-to-cuff junction with contrast stretch specifically to try to find a second pleat): exactly ONE crisp folded pleat edge with a hard shadow line descends into the cuff seam, immediately outboard of the placket. Everything further right is soft diagonal drape shading from the sleeve blousing, not a second fold - no second hard vertical fold edge terminates at the cuff seam anywhere in frame. Count therefore matches the drawing and does NOT substitute the two-pleat sibling geometry.

Counts confirmed: 1 pleat, 1 placket button, 1 cuff button. Placket top is pointed/tower as drawn, with topstitching along both edges. Cuff is a rectangular single-button barrel cuff with edge stitching, matching the drawn cuff. Orientation is the detail exterior face of the lower sleeve, matching the illustration - no opposite-face substitution.

Composition: the cuff/pleat junction is the dominant, unobstructed subject, framed macro; nothing covers the pleat, placket or cuff (no tie, no jacket sleeve). Background is a seamless plain neutral light-grey studio sweep with clear separation - no location, architecture, furniture, scenery or props. Full-frame contrast sweep found NO text, numbers, units, arrows, leader/dimension lines, callouts, red or coloured guide marks, ruler ticks, labels or watermark anywhere in frame; the red annotation line from the tech pack was correctly NOT traced onto the cloth. Real photograph, no line-art or CGI look.

Not scored as defects: cuff depth-to-width ratio cannot be compared directly between a flat pattern drawing and a cuff worn on a wrist (the visible cuff width is a foreshortened cylinder arc, not the flat pattern width). Left/right symmetry is largely inapplicable to a single-sleeve detail; nothing is wrongly asymmetric and the cuff seam reads level.

No Critical or Major discrepancies found. The two logged Minors are a slight inboard bias of the pleat position relative to the drawn gap, and a slightly softened cuff corner - neither changes which craft option a customer would identify, and the defining feature (one pleat) reads correctly within one second.
